summary_en: eSOL's board recommended shareholders accept a tender offer at 820 yen per share by BCJ-110, a special acquisition vehicle backed by Bain Capital Private Equity, with a minimum acceptance threshold of 10.5 million shares (66.67% of voting rights). CEO Gondo Masaki will acquire shares in the parent company and remain involved in business operations post-acquisition.
title_en: Notice Regarding Implementation of MBO and Recommendation for Shareholders to Accept Tender Offer
translation_en_brief:
eSOL's board of directors approved and recommended a management buyout transaction on September 1, 2026, whereby BCJ-110, a special acquisition vehicle established on June 1, 2026, will launch a public tender offer for all outstanding common shares at 820 yen per share. The tender offer period runs from September 2 to October 19, 2026 (30 business days). BCJ-110 is a wholly owned subsidiary of BCJ-109, which is in turn entirely owned by Bain Capital Private Equity, LP and its affiliated investment funds (collectively "Bain Capital"), a global investment firm with approximately 225 billion dollars in assets under management.

The minimum acceptance threshold is 10,535,800 shares, representing 66.67 percent of outstanding voting rights (as of the record date calculated at 197,078 voting rights). Upon successful completion, eSOL will become a wholly owned subsidiary of BCJ-110 and its shares will be delisted from the Tokyo Stock Exchange. CEO Masaki Gondo has agreed to acquire equity interests in the parent company and will continue to be involved in overall business operations following consummation of the transaction. The board determined that the transaction was proposed through mutual agreement between BCJ-110, its parent, and management, satisfying the definition of a management buyout under Tokyo Stock Exchange regulations. The transaction was approved unanimously by all directors without conflicts of interest, including audit committee members.
